source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables

summary: The feature introduces a statistical corrector component (sR) that captures correlations between register values and branch directions. It generates a 12-bit digest for each register value and stores it in a Tomasulo-like table. At prediction time, the component independently selects the most useful available register digest from each of its 8 banks, and uses these digests to index prediction weight tables that contribute to the global branch prediction sum.

state.name: logical_register_table
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits for ROB tag or 12 bits for register digest), decay_ctr (8 bits)

state.name: sR_usefulness_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks. Each bank has 3 tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each.
state.entry_format: Vector of 8 or 9 6-bit saturating counters (one per logical register assigned to the bank)

state.name: sR_prediction_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks. Each bank has 3 tables (WT0, WT1, WT2) of 128, 256, and 512 entries respectively.

algorithms.name: allocate_register_tag
algorithms.notes: Tracks which instruction will produce the next value for the logical register.

algorithms.name: update_register_digest
algorithms.notes: Generates a 12-bit digest. INT: leading ones/zeros count, trailing ones/zeros count, 6 LSBs. FP: format class, sign, exponent MSBs. Flags: 4 bits replicated 3 times.

algorithms.name: decay_register_digest
algorithms.notes: Invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded to prevent stale data from degrading accuracy.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.notes: Picks the digest of the most useful register among those available in each bank and forwards it to the second table (WT).

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.notes: Updates correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time. Randomly selects one available register per bank to update, requiring only a single write port.

host_interfaces.description: The 64-bit value produced by an instruction, along with its register type (INT, FP, Flags), needed to generate the 12-bit digest as early as possible.
host_interfaces.fallback: Provide the register values at commit time, though this limits the predictor to only exploiting values from older, fully committed instructions.

host_interfaces.need: decode signal and destination register ID
host_interfaces.description: Needed to allocate the tag in the logical register table and invalidate the previous digest.
host_interfaces.fallback: Monitor register rename stage instead of decode.

host_interfaces.description: Used as a tag to ensure that when an instruction completes, it only overwrites the payload if it is the most recent writer to that logical register.
host_interfaces.fallback: Use an incrementing instruction sequence number (SQN).

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: 1495 bits for the Tomasulo-like logical register table (65 entries * 23 bits), 9360 bits for the usefulness weight tables (65 regs distributed across 8 banks * 3 tables * 8 entries * 6-bit weights), 43008 bits for the prediction weight tables (8 banks * 3 tables * (128+256+512) entries * 6-bit weights).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Digest generation requires leading/trailing zero counters and bit extraction. Prediction requires finding the maximum usefulness sum among 8 or 9 registers per bank.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: Base TAGE predictor capacity or Bimodal predictor capacity could be reduced to pay for this component at iso-storage.

parameters.name: digest_lifetime
parameters.storage_impact: Dictates the width of the decay counter in the logical register table (e.g., a max of 256 requires an 8-bit counter).

parameters.name: digest_width
parameters.storage_impact: Changes the size of the payload field in the logical register table and the index width for the WT tables.

unit_tests.name: digest_generation_int
unit_tests.given: An INT register is written with a value.
unit_tests.expect: The generated digest encodes the leading zeros/ones count, trailing zeros/ones count, and 6 LSBs into a 12-bit value.

unit_tests.name: decay_mechanism
unit_tests.given: A register value is produced, its valid bit is set, and 256 subsequent instructions are decoded without that register being written again.
unit_tests.expect: The valid bit for that register in the logical register table is cleared.

unit_tests.name: most_useful_selection
unit_tests.given: Multiple registers in the same bank are valid. One has a significantly higher usefulness sum in UT than the others for the current PC.
unit_tests.expect: The predictor selects the digest of the register with the highest usefulness sum to index the WT for that bank.

open_questions: What are the exact bit widths allocated for the leading/trailing zero/one counts in the INT register digest? (Assumed 3 bits each, as the LSBs take 6 bits of the 12-bit digest. Alternative reading: arbitrary distribution of the remaining 6 bits).
How exactly are the format bits, sign bit, and exponent MSBs packed into the 12-bit FP digest? (Assumed a specific concatenation order, but the packing is not explicitly stated).
Are the 65 logical registers distributed evenly across the 8 banks? (Assumed 8 banks of 8 registers, with one bank having 9 registers to total 65, inferred from Figure 5 and Table 3 dimensions).
How exactly are the UT and WT hashed using the PC and digest? (Assumed standard folded XOR hashing).
What is the exact layout of the 14-bit tag in the Tomasulo-like table if the host ROB index is smaller or larger than 14 bits? (Assumed simple truncation or zero-extension).
